description:
`Shale.Pushing.crosses_cut_boundary?/2` (lib/bedrock/data_plane/log/shale/pushing.ex:266-272) hardcodes the module default:

    defp crosses_cut_boundary?(%{min_version: min_version}, version) do
      interval = Demux.Server.default_cut_interval_us()
      div(Version.to_integer(version), interval) > div(Version.to_integer(min_version), interval)
    end

Its own comment states the invariant it is meant to uphold: 'Same version arithmetic as the Demux's deterministic cuts: a segment holds exactly one cut bucket of versions.'

But the demux does NOT use the default - `bucket_of/2` (demux/server.ex:404) uses `state.cut_interval_us`, set from `Keyword.get(opts, :cut_interval_us, @default_cut_interval_us)` and documented as a supported option at demux/server.ex:115.

## Failure scenario

Configure `cut_interval_us` to anything other than 5_000_000 and the two boundaries silently diverge:

- **Configured > default:** the log rolls more often than the demux cuts. Wasteful (extra renames + header writes + fsyncs) but safe.
- **Configured < default:** a single segment spans multiple cut buckets. This breaks the reasoning the roll exists to serve - the active segment is trim-immune, so `available_after` chases the untrimmed tail across bucket boundaries and the trim floor can be computed against a segment that is not yet fully durable.

Nothing configures a non-default interval today, so this is latent. It is a trap for whoever first tunes the knob, and the misleading comment makes it look correct.

## Fix

Thread the demux's configured `cut_interval_us` through to Shale (state or writer_opts) and use it in `crosses_cut_boundary?/2`. Keep the default as the fallback when unset.

## Test (write first, must fail)

Drive `append_transaction/2` with a non-default cut interval and assert the roll boundary matches `Demux.Server.bucket_of/2` arithmetic at that same interval - i.e. a segment holds exactly one bucket. Assert both the smaller-than-default and larger-than-default directions.
title: [BUG] Log segment roll reads the default cut interval, not the demux's configured one
